record.original_question: Among degree-k polynomial threshold functions f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, is the one with maximal total influence always the symmetric threshold f(x) = sgn(p(x_1 + ... + x_n)), where p is a degree-k univariate polynomial alternating sign on the k+1 values of x_1 + ... + x_n closest to 0?

evidence.quote: Statement: Among degree- k polynomial threshold functions f : {-1, 1}^n -> {-1, 1}, the one with maximal total influence is the symmetric one f ( x) = sgn( p( x1 + ... + xn )), where p is a degree- k univariate polynomial which alternates sign on the k + 1 values of x1 + ... + xn closest to 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n, k be positive integers with k ≤ n. A function f : {−1, 1}^n → {−1, 1} is called a degree-k polynomial threshold function (PTF) if there exists a real multilinear polynomial P(x_1, …, x_n) of degree at most k such that f(x) = sgn(P(x)) for all x ∈ {−1, 1}^n (with sgn(0) defined arbitrarily). The total influence (average sensitivity) of f is

  I(f) = ∑_{i=1}^{n} Pr_{x ∼ Unif{−1,1}^n}[f(x) ≠ f(x^{⊕i})],

where x^{⊕i} denotes x with its i-th coordinate flipped.

Consider the symmetric degree-k PTF defined as follows. Let s(x) = x_1 + x_2 + ⋯ + x_n, and let p(t) be a univariate polynomial of degree k chosen so that, on the k+1 values of s(x) closest to 0 (i.e., the k+1 integers in {−n, −n+2, …, n−2, n} of smallest absolute value), the sign of p alternates. Define

  f*(x) = sgn(p(s(x))).

Question: Is it true that, for every n and every k ≤ n, the function f* attains the maximum value of I(f) among all degree-k polynomial threshold functions f : {−1, 1}^n → {−1, 1}?
artifact.status_search_result: This is the Gotsman–Linial conjecture (1991). Brynmor Chapman (arXiv:2108.02288, "The Gotsman–Linial Conjecture is False") refuted the conjecture for almost all degrees d and almost all n, while confirming it in many remaining cases. Hence the answer to the question (that the symmetric PTF always maximizes total influence) is false in general.

status_evidence.title: The Gotsman-Linial Conjecture is False
status_evidence.snippet: Chapman refutes the Gotsman-Linial conjecture for almost all d and almost all n, while confirming it in many of the remaining cases.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture that the symmetric PTF maximizes average sensitivity among degree-k PTFs has been disproved in general.
